get.description:
Finished runs' items as OTLP log requests, oldest first, after a cursor. A plugin inside a
customer's mission control polls this from their side and keeps the last cursor it applied;
naming itself (consumer) lets the platform show when it last pulled, and gets it only the
resources of feed outputs to its connection: a run's entry repeats its items per output.

A bridge that pages (`page_records`) gets an entry with more records than that in pages:
the first here, with `next_page`, and the rest from `cursor=<the entry>&page=<n>`, which it
joins before applying the run. A bridge that does not page always gets whole entries.

A page also stops at FEED_PAGE_BYTES encoded, so `entries` can hold fewer than `limit`:
continue from `next`. An entry alone over that is returned alone with `oversized: true`;
name `page_records` to read it in pages.

`from=latest` is where a first start reads from, without reading a run: no entries, and
`next` just before the newest run with something for `consumer` (the newest entry when none
has), so reading on from it applies that run and none older.

`oldest` is the oldest entry the feed still holds (null when it holds none): entries expire
FEED_TTL after they were published, so a bridge whose cursor sorts before `oldest` may have
missed entries that expired while it was offline.
